criteria.title: System discovery advertises the sidecar-first public bootstrap contract
criteria.assertion: `/api/v1/system/info` must advertise the approved public bootstrap contract through `features.relay_sidecar=true`, `features.relay_read_models=true` when sidecar publishing is enabled, at least one browser bootstrap URL in `nostr.browser_relays` or `nostr.sidecar_url`, and `nostr.service_pubkey` when canonical Bahia-authored read models are expected. While sidecar-first bootstrap is enabled, raw backend `nostr.relays` must not be the approved browser bootstrap surface.
preconditions: System info handler is exercised in a sidecar-enabled configuration with Nostr publication enabled.
A service key is configured for the canonical-author success case.
steps: Request or construct the `/api/v1/system/info` payload for the sidecar-enabled configuration.
Inspect `features`, `nostr.browser_relays`, `nostr.sidecar_url`, `nostr.service_pubkey`, and `nostr.relays`.
criteria.expected_result: The payload advertises the sidecar-first public bootstrap fields required by the approved slice and does not require raw `nostr.relays` for browser bootstrap.
negative_cases: If sidecar-first bootstrap is enabled but the payload omits browser bootstrap URLs or `relay_read_models`, the criterion fails.
If browser bootstrap for the approved path depends on raw `nostr.relays`, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: System discovery advertises conditional control-plane capabilities and legacy fail-closed flags explicitly
criteria.assertion: `/api/v1/system/info.control_plane` must advertise the canonical control-plane version, correlation tags, and request/status/result/read-model kind maps for enabled capabilities only. Optional domains such as LLM and MCP async correlation must disappear when disabled, while removed legacy feature keys (`nostr_auth_exchange`, `legacy_sse`, `legacy_jwt_exchange`, `legacy_agent_http`) remain explicitly `false` so older clients fail closed.
preconditions: System info handler is exercised across enabled and disabled optional-feature configurations.
steps: Construct or request one payload with optional features enabled and one with them disabled.
Inspect `control_plane` capability/kind maps and the legacy feature flags.
criteria.expected_result: Enabled payloads include the corresponding contract surface, disabled payloads omit it, and removed legacy flags remain explicit `false` values.
negative_cases: If disabled optional capabilities are still advertised, the criterion fails.
If removed legacy features disappear or become truthy instead of remaining explicit `false` values, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: System-info loading is shared, cached, deduplicated, and force-refreshable
criteria.assertion: The shared browser system-info store must fetch `/api/v1/system/info` once for normal bootstrap, serve cached discovery data to subsequent consumers, deduplicate concurrent loads into one request, and only refetch when an explicit force reload is requested.
preconditions: The browser store is exercised with a deterministic system-info API mock.
steps: Call `loadSystemInfo()` twice in sequence.
Call `loadSystemInfo()` concurrently from two callers.
Call `loadSystemInfo({ force: true })` after an initial load.
criteria.expected_result: Sequential and concurrent normal loads share one fetch result, while force reload performs a fresh request and replaces cached discovery data.
negative_cases: If repeated normal loads refetch discovery data per consumer, the criterion fails.
If force reload does not replace cached state, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: Shared browser bootstrap uses advertised public discovery, waits for EOSE, then stays live
criteria.assertion: The shared control-plane browser bootstrap must resolve public relay URLs from `nostr.browser_relays` plus `nostr.sidecar_url`, set those relays on the shared Nostr client, connect, query canonical read-model and activity filters until EOSE, apply the returned state, and then open live subscriptions rather than treating the historical query as terminal state.
preconditions: System discovery advertises sidecar-first public bootstrap fields and `relay_read_models=true`.
At least one advertised relay is reachable for the success case.
steps: Bootstrap the shared control-plane store from a deterministic system-info payload.
Observe relay resolution, connection setup, the EOSE-bounded query call, and the subsequent live subscription.
criteria.expected_result: Bootstrap becomes ready only after the initial EOSE-bounded query completes, shared state is populated from the returned events, and the connection status transitions to live with an open live subscription.
negative_cases: If the bootstrap path skips the EOSE-bounded historical query and only subscribes live, the criterion fails.
If the bootstrap path treats the initial query as sufficient and does not open a live subscription, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: Shared browser bootstrap fails closed on missing capability or unreachable public bootstrap
criteria.assertion: The approved browser bootstrap path must fail locally with deterministic discovery or connectivity errors when `features.relay_read_models` is not advertised, when no browser bootstrap URLs are advertised, or when the client cannot connect to any advertised public relay. It must not silently fall back to unsupported shared-state behavior.
preconditions: One test run omits required discovery fields or capability flags.
One test run simulates connection failure for all advertised public relays.
steps: Attempt bootstrap with `relay_read_models=false` or missing.
Attempt bootstrap with no advertised browser bootstrap URLs.
Attempt bootstrap where all advertised public relays fail to connect.
criteria.expected_result: Each invalid bootstrap case returns a deterministic failure and leaves the shared control-plane store in a non-ready error state.
negative_cases: If bootstrap claims readiness without `relay_read_models`, the criterion fails.
If bootstrap falls through to unsupported fallback behavior after public discovery or connection failure, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: Relay-backed shared state applies canonical-author filtering and replaceable latest-wins semantics
criteria.assertion: After bootstrap discovery provides the Bahia service pubkey, the shared control-plane store must ignore canonical Bahia read-model and status/result events from non-service authors, accept only the latest replaceable event for each `(kind, pubkey, d-tag)` identity, and honor tombstones by removing deleted projections from visible state.
preconditions: Bootstrap has already discovered a canonical Bahia service pubkey.
The relay event stream includes stale, current, tombstone, and spoofed canonical events.
steps: Apply older, newer, stale-replay, and tombstone replaceable events for the same entity.
Apply spoofed canonical Bahia events from a non-service author.
Inspect visible shared state collections.
criteria.expected_result: Visible state reflects only the newest valid canonical events, tombstones remove deleted entities, and spoofed canonical Bahia events do not mutate state.
negative_cases: If stale replaceable events overwrite newer state, the criterion fails.
If spoofed canonical Bahia events from non-service authors mutate visible state, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: Live connection state remains reactive after bootstrap
criteria.assertion: Once shared browser bootstrap has completed, the visible connection status must react to disconnect and reconnect signals from the shared Nostr client so the UI can distinguish live, disconnected, and reconnected states without rerunning bootstrap.
preconditions: The shared control-plane store has already completed bootstrap successfully.
steps: Toggle the shared Nostr client connection store from connected to disconnected and back to connected.
Inspect the control-plane connection status and reconnect counter.
criteria.expected_result: The connection state becomes `disconnected` on loss and returns to `live` on reconnection, recording a reconnect after bootstrap completion.
negative_cases: If connection loss leaves the store claiming `live`, the criterion fails.
If reconnection requires a fresh bootstrap to restore `live` state, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: Operator CLI relay resolution uses explicit inputs first and system discovery second
criteria.assertion: Signer-first operator relay resolution must use `--relay` first, then `BAHIA_NOSTR_RELAYS`, and only then fall back to `/api/v1/system/info` discovery using the sidecar-first public bootstrap fields. If system discovery is used and provides no browser bootstrap URLs, the CLI must fail with a deterministic error instead of inventing relay targets.
preconditions: The operator CLI has access to one test case for each precedence branch: explicit flags, environment variable, and system discovery fallback.
steps: Resolve relays with explicit `--relay` flags.
Resolve relays with `BAHIA_NOSTR_RELAYS` and no explicit flags.
Resolve relays from `/api/v1/system/info` when no other source is present.
Resolve relays from `/api/v1/system/info` when discovery advertises no browser bootstrap URLs.
criteria.expected_result: Each precedence branch is respected exactly, and the discovery fallback uses only the approved public bootstrap fields with deterministic failure when they are absent.
negative_cases: If system discovery overrides explicit flags or environment values, the criterion fails.
If discovery fallback succeeds without browser bootstrap URLs, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: Encrypted capability remains separately gated and must not be inferred from public bootstrap
criteria.assertion: System discovery may advertise encrypted-request capability for other browser domains, but that capability must remain explicitly gated and separately discoverable. Public bootstrap fields alone (`browser_relays`, `sidecar_url`, or other public bootstrap metadata) must not imply encrypted capability, and consumers of this slice must not treat the public bootstrap path as sufficient proof of encrypted messaging support.
preconditions: One discovery payload advertises only public bootstrap fields.
One discovery payload advertises public bootstrap fields plus the encrypted capability indicators used by the implementation.
steps: Inspect the public-only discovery payload and evaluate whether encrypted capability would be inferred.
Inspect the payload with explicit encrypted capability indicators and confirm the public bootstrap path remains separate.
criteria.expected_result: Public bootstrap metadata does not, by itself, authorize or imply encrypted capability; encrypted capability is separately gated when present.
negative_cases: If encrypted capability becomes true from public bootstrap fields alone, the criterion fails.
If consumers of this slice treat the public bootstrap path as proof of encrypted messaging support, the criterion fails.

criteria.title: Raw `nostr.relays` exposure is not an approved bootstrap success path for this slice
criteria.assertion: The approved `SYSTEM_DISCOVERY_RELAY_BOOTSTRAP` slice does not consider sidecar-disabled raw `nostr.relays` exposure a valid browser bootstrap success path. Tests or clients that satisfy this slice must prove sidecar-first bootstrap behavior rather than relying on direct `nostr.relays` normalization as equivalent behavior.
preconditions: A sidecar-disabled discovery configuration exists for comparison against the approved sidecar-first path.
steps: Inspect bootstrap behavior and test assumptions for the approved slice.
Compare them against a sidecar-disabled configuration that exposes raw `nostr.relays`.
criteria.expected_result: The approved slice treats sidecar-first bootstrap as the required path and does not accept raw `nostr.relays` exposure as equivalent proof.
negative_cases: If the acceptance set can be satisfied entirely by raw `nostr.relays` fallback behavior, the criterion fails.
If sidecar-disabled raw `nostr.relays` exposure is silently treated as approved browser bootstrap behavior, the criterion fails.
